questions.question: How many bits are in an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: IPv4 addresses consist of four 8-bit octets.

questions.question: Which decimal value cannot appear as an IPv4 address octet?
A packet leaves a host with IPv4 TTL 64 and passes three forwarding routers. Each subtracts one. What TTL arrives at the destination?
questions.explanation: The packet's TTL decreases by one per forwarding router in this scenario. 64 minus three gives 61.

questions.question: Which IPv4 header field indicates that the payload is ICMP?
questions.explanation: The Protocol field identifies the encapsulated protocol. ICMP is protocol number 1.

questions.question: A capture shows IPv4 Total Length 84 and IHL 5. How many bytes follow the IPv4 header inside the datagram?
questions.explanation: IHL counts 32-bit words, so five words form a 20-byte header. Subtract the header from the total length to get 64 bytes.

questions.question: A host formerly obtained its address, prefix and router through DHCP. After conversion to static settings it reaches local peers, but it has no route to remote networks. Which missing setting explains the behavior?
questions.explanation: A usable static address and mask allow on-link communication. A default gateway supplies a next hop for other destinations.

questions.question: Besides an address, which useful pair can an IPv4 DHCP server supply to a client?

options.B: Switch port duplex and fiber connector
options.C: TCP acknowledgment number and receive window

questions.explanation: DHCP options can supply the client mask and default-router information.

questions.question: Why is the IPv4 header checksum updated by a forwarding router even when the payload stays the same?

options.A: The destination IP is replaced with the gateway IP
options.B: Forwarding changes a header field such as TTL
options.C: The TCP ports always change at each hop
options.D: The checksum covers the Ethernet source address

questions.explanation: The checksum protects the IPv4 header, so a TTL change requires an update.

questions.question: A router receives an IPv4 packet with TTL 1 that would otherwise be forwarded. What normally occurs?

options.A: The packet is forwarded unchanged as a broadcast
options.B: The packet is discarded and the router may send ICMP Time Exceeded
options.C: The router sends a TCP reset to the destination
options.D: The router forwards it with TTL 255

questions.explanation: Forwarding would exhaust TTL, so the packet is dropped. ICMP Time Exceeded can report this condition.

questions.question: A workstation was switched from static settings to DHCP and no lease was obtained. Which first check directly tests whether the intended address source exists on that network?

options.A: Check whether the address in the old manual entry is in DNS
options.B: Verify that a DHCP service or relay is available for the LAN
options.C: Compare the manual gateway with the switch's MAC aging timer
options.D: Inspect the peer's TCP receive window

questions.explanation: A DHCP client needs a reachable DHCP service, directly or through a relay.
